name: Railroad Crossbuck
spec: white X-shaped crossbuck with black legend RAILROAD CROSSING on the two arms
meaning: You are at the tracks; yield to any train, stop if one is coming.

snippets.back: At a railroad crossbuck or warning sign, prepare to stop for trains.
Red flashing lights work with crossbuck signs at many railroad crossings, and you must always stop when they begin flashing because a train is near, checking every track before you cross.
The railroad crossbuck is a white X-shaped sign with black lettering located at the crossing.
Treat a railroad crossbuck like a yield sign, and a sign below it shows how many tracks the crossing has when there is more than one.
The yellow X warns from afar, the white crossbuck yields at the rails, and gates with blinkers jail wheels until arms rise and lamps die, three rail guards in rising command.
The railroad emergency notification number is normally on a blue sign at the crossbuck or near the crossing.
Advance signs preview crossings, crossbucks yield with track counts, flashing reds stop at once, gates never bypass, paint marks the halt, and X envelopes flag the strike zone.
At a railroad crossbuck, slow, look and listen and yield to an approaching train. A panel beneath the crossbuck identifies the number of tracks.
